rate_limit.note: oauth.v2.access is documented at 600/min [C-SL-25]; the demo makes single-digit calls.

_notes.scopes: 18 user-token scopes, one per command in SLACK-COMMAND-SPEC §4 — every string verified against docs.slack.dev/reference/scopes/ that review, and every one traceable to a named command (no speculative scope reaches the consent screen, §6 of docs/registration/SLACK.md). Grown from the Phase-1 three (channels:read, channels:history, users:read) on 2026-08-17. Slack scopes are ADDITIVE-ONLY [C-SL-31]: the next engine.connect('slack') sends the full user_scope list and the user sees ONE Allow screen; the old token is superseded, not stacked. No dashboard change, no new registration — desktop PKCE apps request user scopes at authorize time. Deliberately absent: groups:write, im:write.topic, mpim:write.topic, usergroups:* — this catalog never manages membership or topics.
_notes.client_id: The one value you paste. Filled from api.slack.com/apps -> Basic Information -> App Credentials -> Client ID. Public config, safe to commit. The Client Secret is never copied, never stored, never sent. NOTE: this file contains a SECOND empty string on purpose — extra_authorize_params.scope — see below.
_notes.scope_param: Slack splits bot vs user scopes across two authorize params. Desktop redirects (localhost + PKCE) MAY NOT request bot scopes [C-SL-03], so we send user_scope only and keep `scope` present-and-empty, mirroring Slack's own PKCE example URL. That deliberate empty string is why 'client_id is the only blank' was never true for Slack (§A16 amends W3's criterion to `_placeholders`).
_notes.scope_delimiter: Slack's own authorize examples comma-separate scope lists; Zoom/Reddit use a space. One axis, no engine branch.
_notes.token_path: For a user-token install the token is nested under authed_user, NOT at the top level. Top-level access_token is the bot token, which this app never has [C-SL-07].
_notes.refresh_auth: U1 CLOSED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-16 (live probe, this Mac): grant_type=refresh_token + refresh_token + client_id in body, NO Authorization header, NO client_secret -> ok:true with a rotated 12h/43200s pair. The rotation page's client_secret-required claim does NOT apply to PKCE public clients; the PKCE page wins. ⚠️ RESPONSE SHAPE DIFFERS FROM EXCHANGE: refresh returns access_token/refresh_token at the TOP LEVEL (scope gains 'identify'), while exchange nests them under authed_user — refresh.ts must parse top-level, see DISCOVERIES.md D-2026-08-16-1.
_notes.refresh_ttl: 2592000s = 30 days. PKCE apps: 'all refresh tokens issued to your app will expire in 30 days instead of lasting indefinitely.' [C-SL-27]
_notes.access_token_ttl: 43200s = 12h, fixed by Slack when token rotation is on. 'It will always expire in 43,200 seconds, which is 12 hours.' [C-SL-09] — re-confirmed live 2026-08-16.
_notes.rotation: optional-enabled = NOT forced for us (localhost redirect), turned ON deliberately at registration so a refresh token exists at all (§A1). Forced rotation is scoped to custom URI schemes [C-SL-34].
_notes.success_predicate: Slack returns failures as HTTP 200 + {"ok": false} [C-SL-20], so the status code alone is never the verdict here.
